candidates.name: Food safety & quality
candidates.day: You check that food is made safely and that the rules are followed. You walk through kitchens or production lines, take samples, keep records and explain what needs to change.

candidates.name: Buying & suppliers
candidates.day: You decide what a company buys, compare prices, talk to suppliers and make sure the right ingredients arrive on time.

candidates.name: Production planning
candidates.day: In a large kitchen or food factory, you plan what gets made each day, how much, and by whom. When an order changes, you sort out the plan.

candidates.name: Recipe & product development
candidates.day: You invent and test new dishes or products for a food company or a chain, write the recipes down exactly, and adjust them until they work in large amounts.

candidates.name: Teaching & training
candidates.day: You teach cooking at a college, in a training kitchen or to new staff. You plan sessions, show techniques and help people get better.

candidates.name: Sales & customer care for food suppliers
candidates.day: You look after restaurants and shops that buy from a food supplier. You visit them, take orders, suggest products and fix problems.

candidates.name: Events & catering planning
candidates.day: You plan the food for weddings, conferences or festivals: menus, staff, timings and suppliers. On the day, you keep it all running.

candidates.name: Cooking in schools, hospitals & care homes
candidates.day: You still cook, but in daytime hours. You plan menus for people with different needs, such as allergies or soft diets, and run a small team.

candidates.name: Food photography & content
candidates.day: You photograph, film or write about food for a brand, a magazine or social media. You style dishes, plan shoots and edit.

candidates.name: Running a café or canteen
candidates.day: You keep a café, a hotel kitchen or a staff canteen running smoothly: rotas, stock, costs, cleanliness and the team.
